paper.title_en: Exact dynamics of spinning particles and the spin wall in Schwarzschild spacetime
paper.abstract_en: The motion of a spinning test body is governed by the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon equations and deviates from geodesics already at first order in the spin. Most studies of this problem truncate the dynamics at linear order; here we solve the equatorial, spin-aligned problem in Schwarzschild spacetime at all orders in the spin under the Tulczyjew--Dixon condition. Eliminating the four-velocity casts the system into a closed algebraic form and reduces the motion to a single first-order radial equation. Keeping track of both kinematical masses, the norm of the four-momentum and its projection on the velocity, we find that the representative worldline ceases to be timelike on a surface in the space of radius, spin and angular momentum. We call this surface the spin wall. It bounds the radii accessible to a spinning body and is present for every nonvanishing value of the momentum's angular component; only for the purely radial family does it collapse, and that family moves on a geodesic. Its position follows in closed form and may lie inside the horizon, enclose it, or reach the exterior, the last possibility arising already at small spin. We also examine how far the pole--dipole truncation remains under control where the wall is accessible. Within that regime we determine the circular orbits and their stability, the spin dependence of the marginally stable orbit, and the perihelion advance beyond first order in the spin.
